Standard: The AR system interface, its attachment to airframe structure, and the structure surrounding the interface withstands the loads experienced during the AR process. a. Boom Tanker. The loads used in the design of the boom refueling system include the maximum, minimum, and most critical combination of loads that can result from contact, disconnect, boom strike, tension disconnect, in-contact axial and radial loads, with and without boom operator input, throughout disconnect envelope, fuel transfer and aerodynamic loads during stow, deploy, and maneuvering throughout the airspeed and altitude refueling envelope, including a tension load of 9,411 lbs applied to the boom-nozzle ball joint when fully extended. b. Drogue Tanker. The loads used in the design of the drogue refueling system include the maximum and most critical combination of loads that can result from hose extension, contact, engagement, hose response, disengagement, off-center engagement, off-center disengagement, fuel transfer, and aerodynamic loads when stowed, trailed, or in transition. The refueling hose design limit tension load is defined by the maximum aerodynamic drag of the hose, fuel reception coupling and drogue of the system at the maximum design operating dynamic pressure for the system or 1,500 lbs for up to a 2- inch inner diameter hose and 2,000 lbs for an over 2-inch diameter hose, whichever load is higher. The coupling DLLs are as follows: 1. 1,500 lbs tension load in combination with a 1,500 lbs radial load. 2. 2,500 lbs compression load with a 1,500 lbs radial load. 3. 1,500 lbs tension load. 4. 2,500 lbs compression load. 5. 1,500 lbs radial load. c. Receptacle Receiver. The loads used in the design of the receptacle refueling system include the maximum, minimum, and most critical combination of loads that can result from engagement, disengagement, tension disconnect, boom strike, fuel transfer, and aerodynamic loads when receptacle is open, closed, and in transition. Design receptacle loads are as follows and are applied within the refueling envelope and disconnect envelope for targeted tanker boom subsystems: 1. Tension: a load of 9,411 lbs applied to the boom-nozzle ball joint. 2. Compression: a load of 9,411 lbs applied to the boom-nozzle ball joint. 3. Air vehicle skin area 12 inches out from receptacle perimeter:1,800 lbs vertical combined with 750 lbs lateral. 4. Aerodynamic loads: Slipway and its doors in both the open and closed positions. d. Probe Receiver. The loads used in the design of the probe refueling system include the maximum, minimum, and most critical combination of loads that can result from engagement, disengagement, off-center disconnect, hose tension, fuel transfer and aerodynamic loads when AR equipment is stowed, deployed, and in transition. Design limit probe loads are as follows: 1. 1,500 lbs tension. 2. 2,500 lbs compression. 3. 1,500 lbs radial. 4. 2,500 lbs compression with 1,500 lbs radial. 5. 1,500 lbs tension with 1,500 lbs radial. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Stress and CFD analyses define limit loads due to AR load cases and aerodynamic environment. Structural analysis verifies boom structure and its attachment to the air vehicle can withstand defined limit loads. b. Drogue Tanker. Stress and CFD analyses define limit loads due to AR load cases and aerodynamic environment. Structural analysis verifies AR system, components, and attachment structure can withstand defined limit loads. c. Receptacle Receiver. Stress and CFD analyses define limit loads due to AR load cases and aerodynamic environment. Structural analysis verifies AR receptacle and surrounding structure can withstand defined limit loads. d. Probe Receiver. Stress and CFD analyses define limit loads due to AR load cases and aerodynamic environment. Structural analysis verifies AR probe and surrounding structure can withstand defined limit loads. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Component qualification laboratory testing verifies boom components and structure can withstand application of DLLs without detrimental deformation. Laboratory testing of integrated boom subsystem demonstrates loads during telescope extension and retraction and contact and disconnect with representative receptacle interface do not exceed DLLs. b. Drogue Tanker. Laboratory testing demonstrates hose extension, hose retraction and hose response loads with representative receiver interface do not exceed limit loads. Component qualification laboratory testing demonstrates the refueling coupling and drogue can withstand DLLs. c. Receptacle Receiver. Component qualification laboratory testing verifies receptacle system and representative support structure can withstand DLLs. d. Probe Receiver. Component qualification laboratory testing verifies probe system and representative support structure can withstand DLLs. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Flight test validates load cases match analytically developed DLLs.
